attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post. He mentions Zitron only as sharing the economics discussion, not as a source he is quoting.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps both parts: what the scaling debate is about, and that the hybrid axis (AlphaFold 3 combining classical and generative AI) has seen far less investment. It is a descriptive observation with no hedge, so it can be scored.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary: the debate is about whether data and compute scaling gets generative AI to AGI, and 'far less investment' means a substantial funding gap. Requiring comparable investment categories is fair and does not stretch the claim either way. The open boundaries of the categories are flagged.

evidence.note: Amodei's November 2024 interview falls in the period and confirms that scaling meant bigger networks, more data and more compute. That backs the debate characterization only in part: it is one participant, and he is not arguing about AGI as such.

The Nature abstract calls AlphaFold 3 a 'single unified deep-learning framework' with a diffusion-based architecture. That cuts somewhat against the classical-plus-generative framing but does not rule out classical components. Nothing on investment.

Developer blog: a generative diffusion model replaced the custom geometry module, and AlphaFold 2 outputs were used for distillation training. This confirms the generative part but does not show a classical-AI component. Nothing on funding.
Sector-wide generative AI funding for 2023, from Quid data via the AI Index. There is no comparable total for the hybrid category, so the claimed funding gap cannot be checked.

reviews.rationale: Only part of the debate characterization is supported, by one participant's statement. The technical sources confirm AlphaFold 3 is generative but neither establish nor rule out a classical component. The decisive investment comparison has no comparable hybrid funding figures: e4 covers generative AI funding only. The packet does not settle the claim.
